claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr is single-phase BCC in the as-sintered state.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The compositional complexity of equimolar WTaTiVZr produces severe local lattice distortions and a heterogeneous energy landscape.
The lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr increase edge-dislocation density and activity.
At high temperature, edge-dislocation mechanisms become more important than screw-dislocation mechanisms in BCC high-entropy alloys.
Edge dislocations in WTaTiVZr have lower high-temperature glide activation barriers than the relevant screw dislocations.
Pure tungsten is governed by sluggish screw-dislocation motion under the stated conditions.
Screw-dislocation-controlled deformation contributes to pure tungsten's high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
A shift toward edge-dislocation activity facilitates more uniform plastic deformation in WTaTiVZr.
A shift toward edge-dislocation activity delays brittle fracture in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed dislocation shift lowers the effective ductile-to-brittle transition temperature of WTaTiVZr.
The proposed dislocation shift increases energy absorption during deformation.
Under identical high-temperature testing, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater elongation or creep strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature testing, WTaTiVZr will absorb more energy before fracture than pure tungsten.
The superior plastic response of WTaTiVZr will be accompanied by edge-dislocation-dominated plasticity.
The proposed mechanism operates primarily at temperatures of at least 1000 degrees Celsius.
Phase instability during prolonged exposure or irradiation-induced defects could suppress the proposed intrinsic dislocation mechanism.
Fusion plasma-facing materials experience severe heat loading and high-energy neutron exposure.
Matching the two materials' microstructural scales while comparing their mechanical response and dislocation populations will isolate the lattice-distortion mechanism.
